![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221961/assets/a5f23af5dd514a65937eee29bb0992ff94d68897d8c6422fcf215aad45379c4a.png)

Consider the part of parabola and constant vector field $F$ shown above. Let $C$ be the path where the part of parabola is traversed from $A$ to $B.$ Which of the following statements are true?

I. ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$

II. ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0$

III. ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ gives the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along $C:$

- If the force works *with* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force helps to push the particle along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- If the force works *against* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force impedes the motion of the particle as it moves along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

With that in mind, let's check each statement.

- Statements I is false, while statement II is true. As the particle moves from $A$ to $B,$ the force $F$ works with the particle for $y<0,$ while $F$  works against the particle for $y>0.$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221961/assets/537aca6190fc2f3e06e85c0781a8bb461559ef0a7515ee29aca505f9d615f820.png)

 

By symmetry, the contribution to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ for $y<0$ is canceled out by the contribution for $y>0.$ So,

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0.
$$

- Statement III is false. If we reverse the orientation of $C,$ then the situation with regards to the work done by $F$ is similar to the previous case.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221961/assets/4939f9a22400a7a56eaeacb77d520e522f50aa8378ca1014a19810122e12da51.png)

 

So, ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
